s1.syndrome_frame: A congenital, exophytic, smooth, and soft lesion on the dorsal tongue
salient_findings: 1.5-cm diameter lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion has been present since birth
Lesion appears partly fatty on MRI
key_facts: 20-year-old man with no significant medical history
1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion has been present since birth
Lesion has not changed in size or character
Vital signs are within normal limits
MRI shows a 1.5-cm protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue
Lesion appears partly fatty, likely submucosal
Lesion demonstrates mild contrast enhancement
Intact overlying mucosa
No involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles
Sublingual space and major salivary glands appear normal

shortlist.label: Choristoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign, congenital tumor with normal tissue

shortlist.label: Hamartoma of the tongue
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital, benign tumor on the tongue

raw.rationale: The lesion appears partly fatty on MRI, which is consistent with a lipoma, and its long-standing presence since birth without change suggests a benign nature

rejected.label: Leiomyomatous hamartoma
rejected.why: Less likely due to the partly fatty appearance on MRI, which is not typical for leiomyomatous hamartoma

rejected.label: Choristoma
rejected.why: Choristoma is a rare tumor that contains normal tissue in an abnormal location, but the description does not strongly suggest this diagnosis

rejected.label: Fibrous epithelial polyp
rejected.why: The lesion's partly fatty appearance and lack of description suggesting a fibrous or epithelial component make this less likely

rejected.label: Hamartoma of the tongue
rejected.why: While possible, the specific mention of the lesion appearing partly fatty leans more towards a lipoma
